question: Does the trained bounding-box tree cause the exposed filtered-query slowdown by traversing rows before applying metadata eligibility?
evidence: DEEP calibration reports documentIndexTrained=true before/after maintenance, false after 200 mutations and reopen. Filtered median latency is much higher in the trained states. This is correlation until the same-store counterfactual is run.
inputs: The already exposed 100K COCO/DEEP train vectors and first 32 calibration queries only. Do not open test.f32 or any held-out query.
comparison: Same in-memory DocumentStore, immutable corpus and query; alternate original trained DenseIndex versus the existing exact postings scan by temporarily disabling only dense_index in an isolated test. Same score implementation, complete metadata filtering, payload, k=10, candidate limit=100 and minimum=-1. No product-code change or new search algorithm.
checks: All fields of every result must match the existing exact scan. Save every query's paired timings, source hashes and index dimensions. Independently count production tree metadata-predicate visits and exact vector dots for the same query/filter; no replicated tree algorithm.
interpretation: Shared-host development diagnosis, not original research, competitor qualification or a performance claim. Existing calibration/soak binaries stay frozen. Any serving fix requires its own validation and new qualification source receipts.
resources: Run only after macOS C-family checks finish, which already wait for native Python and guest SDK checks; two Cargo build jobs. No Intel-soak workload or paid service.
